## feature

<!-- New capability this task added. -->

### secondary records excluded from every metric

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The full suite passes with a new end-to-end test, and the guard sites are
covered by both updated pinned tests and the new test.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The four record loops now skip secondary (`0x100`) records before any
   tally or tag work: annotate (`lib.py:270`), error-stats (`lib.py:431`),
   pileup (`lib.py:489`), and qc-summary (`lib.py:554`).
2. Annotate still writes secondary records to the output BAM, untagged, so
   the pass-through stays record-complete.
3. The qc-summary length-dist gate dropped its own secondary test
   (`not is_supplementary` alone remains) because the shared loop guard
   now drops secondary records first.
4. `usage.qmd` states the new universe in three places, and the
   qc-summary CLI docstring names it; the version is 0.9.0.

#### before

A read with k secondary placements counted k times in `total_reads`,
strand, FL, on_target, AP, per-read error counts, and depth. The
samtools-depth parity held only on BAMs without secondary records.

#### after

Every metric counts each read once, at its primary alignment. The parity
condition shrinks to QC-fail (`0x200`) and duplicate (`0x400`) records.
Supplementary (`0x800`) records remain included, as before.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic, text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `src/sam_tagger/lib.py:270,431,489,554` — the four guards.
- New test `tests/test_complex.py::test_secondary_records_excluded_from_metrics_and_passed_through`
  (per_read total 1, per_base total 28, pileup dp set `{1}`, secondary
  record written untagged, FL stats `{"seq1": 1, "seq2": 0}`).
- Suite output: `171 passed in 2.61s`; ruff: `All checks passed!`;
  pyright: `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations`.
- Updated pinned tests: `tests/test_qc_summary.py:285-288` (total 3,
  forward 1, reverse 2) and `tests/test_qc_summary.py:347` (total 4).
- Commits: `f835487` (feat!), `d9f3172` (docs), `cfa0cbc` (0.9.0 bump).

:::

## assumption

<!-- Unverified premise the work depends on. -->

### samtools depth keeps supplementary and drops secondary by default

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The claim was verified from bam2depth source during an earlier task and is
recorded in the audit trail, but it was not re-verified against samtools
source this turn.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The parity benefit of this change rests on samtools depth's default
   record filter: it drops unmapped, secondary, QC-fail, and duplicate
   records, and keeps supplementary records.
2. Given that premise, dropping secondary removes one of sam-tagger's
   three documented divergence sources, and dropping supplementary would
   have created a new one.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `docs/misc/requirements_audit.qmd:401` — "samtools semantics verified
  from cloned source (bam2depth.c line-cited)".
- `tests/test_integration.py:518-525` — the parity test docstring records
  the same default-filter claim.

:::

## conclusion

<!-- Interpreted claim: what we now know. -->

### the tool now enforces its own stated principle everywhere

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The code, the tests, and the documentation now state the same record
universe, verified by the suite this turn.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The length-dist rationale ("secondary records double-count reads")
   now applies to every metric, not only distributions.
2. The `forward_reads + reverse_reads == total_reads` invariant survives
   because all three columns share the new guard.
3. Supplementary records in read-level counts (`total_reads`, FL,
   on_target, AP) stay included and remain an open design question.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `docs/usage.qmd` — depth-universe, strand-counts, and length-dist
  sections now carry the same universe statement.
- `tests/test_qc_summary.py:289-290` — the invariant assertion still
  holds under the new counts.

:::

## observation

<!-- What was noticed in data or behavior, without interpretation. -->

### bare pixi run test resolves pytest from the global pixi bin

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The resolution was verified directly with `pixi run which pytest` this
session.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `pixi run test` in the default environment ran
  `/bioproj/tools/share/.pixi/bin/pytest`, not a project-env pytest,
  because the default environment declares no pytest.
2. That pytest cannot import `sam_tagger`, so all 13 test files failed at
   collection with `ModuleNotFoundError`.
3. `pixi run -e dev test` resolves the dev-env pytest and passes.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `pixi run python -c ...` resolves `.pixi/envs/default/bin/python`;
  `pixi run which pytest` resolves `/bioproj/tools/share/.pixi/bin/pytest`.
- `pixi.toml` — pytest is declared only under
  `[environments.dev.dependencies]`/`[feature.dev.pypi-dependencies]`.

:::

## process

<!-- Audit of a significant action or decision between plan and report. -->

### ran the suite with bare pixi run test first

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. I ran `pixi run test` before checking which environment supplies
   pytest, and all 13 files failed at collection.
2. The `ModuleNotFoundError` pointed at a broken install, not the real
   cause, so one `pixi install` was wasted on a healthy environment.
3. The better action was to resolve the interpreter first
   (`pixi run which pytest`), then use `pixi run -e dev test`.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- Command outputs quoted under `## observation` above.

:::

### shipped the new test with two wrong expectations

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The first version expected one pileup row (actual: 28, one per
   position) and omitted the FL-stats zero-fill row for a header-only
   reference.
2. Both misses came from writing expectations without reading the
   writers' output contracts first.
3. The better action was to model the assertions on the existing
   `test_error_stats_generation` and `read_simple_stats` behavior before
   running.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- Two consecutive failures of
  `test_secondary_records_excluded_from_metrics_and_passed_through`,
  then `171 passed` after the fixes.

:::
